title: The Magic Cup Club
teaser: Nothing up the sleeve, and every single cup is a winner.
clue: A very small show with a very short act list, and no empty seat in the house.
reveal: Put on a tiny magic show where every cup hides a surprise. Your dog picks, you reveal with a flourish, and a slow swap adds a little mystery for the dogs who enjoy it. Kids can be the magician.
objective: Perform three short acts with light, upturned cups where each one hides something, then finish with a favorite toy.
instructions: Set up on a non-slip rug. You need three light, unbreakable cups or tubs with wide, smooth rims and flat bottoms (yoghurt tubs work). No glass, ceramic, lids or tall narrow cups. They are only ever used upside down.
Prepare three small surprises so that no cup is empty: a favorite toy, a few pieces of the day's ration, and a plain cloth bigger than your dog's mouth.
Act one, the reveal: with your dog watching, set a single cup over the toy. Wait. Any sniff, nudge or paw counts. If your dog is unsure, lift the cup yourself with a 'ta-da'.

Act two, the three cups: set all three surprises under three cups a hand's width apart and step back. Your dog picks whichever they like. Lift the others yourself and let them see each one. A 'wrong' cup is just another prize.

Act three, the shuffle (optional, only for dogs who are enjoying it): slide two cups past each other once, slowly and in plain view, and let your dog choose. If they are puzzled, just lift the cup for them.
Finale: put the favorite toy under a towel, wave a hand, say your magic word, and let your dog uncover it. Play a minute and end on that.
Take a bow and put the cups away out of reach.
twist: The magician never lets the dog lose: every cup hides something, so any choice is a good one, and the difficulty only rises as far as your dog wants.
variations: For a beginner or a puppy: do act one only, with one cup, and lift it yourself.
For a seated owner: set the cups on a low tray in front of your chair.
For a food-free show: hide a toy, a scrap of cloth and a toy that crinkles gently, with no ration at all.
For a family: let a child be the magician while an adult sits next to the dog.
completion: Your dog has investigated at least one cup and the finale toy has been found.
photoIdea: Photograph the three upturned cups with your dog's nose in the frame, or the moment a cup tips over.
memoryPrompt: Which cup did your dog choose first, and what did they find?
supplies: Three light plastic cups or tubs
optionalSupplies: A few pieces of today's ration
substitutes: No tubs? Use three sturdy paper cups, replacing any your dog chews.
dietNotes: Any ration is only a few pieces counted from today's food. Ask your vet about your dog's diet. The food-free version uses toys and cloth only.
safety: Use cups with no lids, always upside down, and never anything your dog can wedge on a muzzle.
Take away any cup your dog starts to chew, and keep them out of reach afterwards.
Keep it short and stop while your dog still wants more.
